issues.description: The problem statement/documentation uses two different identifiers for the animal feeding method, creating a naming inconsistency: the UML and several task descriptions declare an abstract method named 'messageOnFeed()', while other textual instructions (the Seal/Pig/Goat task descriptions and the feedAllAnimals specification) refer to 'getFeedingSound()'. The reference solution implements and uses messageOnFeed() (see Animal.java and Farm.java), so the mixed naming in the problem text can confuse students about which method name to implement and which name the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() consistently (update problem_statement.md to replace all getFeedingSound() occurrences with messageOnFeed()), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the code and all solution/tests to getFeedingSound(). Ensure the UML, textual tasks, template comments, and tests all reference the same identifier so students are not confused about which method to implement and call.
